turns.text: Hey Lloyd, did you see that weather alert for tomorrow? Looks like a storm.
I saw the forecast, Alan. It looks like heavy rain is expected in the afternoon. You might want to bring an umbrella.
Thanks. Also, I was looking into that new open-source model everyone is talking about.
Which one are you referring to?
The 26B. I read that 26B has 26B total parameters with a 4B active footprint.
That's an efficient design. It likely balances capacity and inference speed well.
Exactly. Anyway, do you have any dinner recommendations for tonight? I'm craving Italian.
There's a place on 4th street that has good reviews for their pasta.
Lloyd, my printer is jamming again. Any quick fixes?
Have you tried checking the paper tray for misaligned sheets? That's a common cause.
Yeah, that helped. It's working now. On another note, I was digging into the architecture of that 26B model we mentioned before.
Oh, the one with the sparse activation? What did you find?
Turns out 26B is a Gemma 4 model size using a Mixture-of-Experts architecture.
MoE makes sense for that parameter count. It explains the active parameter efficiency.
Right. I also need to order some replacement ink. Can you remind me to do that tomorrow?
I've added that to your task list for tomorrow morning.
